headline: Starship Makes Its First Tower Catch
lede: Flight 15 put 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit, then brought Starship home for a controlled landing between the launch tower’s mechanical arms. The booster’s fuel trouble complicates the triumph, but the spacecraft’s recovery marks a consequential step toward rapid reuse.

headline: Apollo’s “Grenade Launcher” Was a Flare Gun
lede: The suspicious-looking device was not lunar artillery. It was a signaling gun, packed to help astronauts announce their position after an emergency landing far from the planned recovery zone.

headline: AI-Built Apps Leave Private Data Unlocked
lede: Researchers examined 159,041 Lovable-built applications and found unauthenticated databases containing passports, contracts, payment records, and private messages. AI can assemble an app quickly; it does not make access controls safe by default.

headline: DRAM Price-Fixing Case Survives Dismissal
lede: A federal judge will let an antitrust suit against Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron proceed. The ruling is not a finding of liability, but synchronized supply cuts and soaring memory prices now face closer scrutiny.

headline: Rust Service Keeps Distributed IDs Gapless
lede: tsoracle provides strictly increasing timestamps and durable integer sequences for distributed systems. Consensus-backed allocation survives crashes and failover without duplicates, regressions, or quietly skipped invoice numbers.

headline: A Dismissal Notice Survives in Fired Clay
lede: A roof slate from Staffordshire preserves a handwritten message apparently dismissing a pottery worker named John Lewis. Inscribed before the tile was fired, it carries one ordinary workplace moment across two centuries.

headline: NetBSD Encrypts More Than the Home Directory
lede: A practical NetBSD guide moves sensitive data across encrypted `/usr`, `/var`, and `/home` volumes while leaving a small root system available for boot and verification. Argon2id, CGD, and careful recovery planning make the boundary explicit: secrecy has operational costs.

headline: Woz Built BASIC Before the Apple I
lede: Integer BASIC did not wait for finished hardware. Wozniak planned and hand-assembled 6502 code, using paper, available machines, and incremental tools to shape software around a computer that was still being built.

headline: The NES Homebrew Era Is Still Growing
lede: Twenty-five modern games show the NES as a living medium rather than a sealed museum piece. Developers work within strict eight-bit limits while adding new ideas, peripherals, polished design, and sometimes fresh cartridges.

headline: Fifteen Semicircles Find a Tighter Home
lede: A visualizer, hill climbing, and Codex-assisted search turned an obscure packing puzzle into a hands-on experiment. The resulting arrangement reached a top-three leaderboard position with an enclosing-circle radius of 2.94853.
